chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Baraqi, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakkūnī, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
The hand is not cut off except for one who broke into a house or broke a lock.

key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: is cut off (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for cutting the hand of a thief in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Ishtibār clarifies the juristic consensus that the hadd punishment of hand amputation is restricted to theft from a 'hirz' (a secured, private place) where the thief breaks in or breaks a lock, distinguishing it from open theft. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on strict evidentiary conditions for hadd penalties to prevent arbitrary application, ensuring the punishment is reserved for clear, deliberate intrusion into protected property.
